name: Government Issue
label: Dischord
lede: [[John Stabb]] outlasted almost a dozen bandmates in nine years, and Government Issue kept changing its sound whether the hardcore kids liked it or not.

eras.title: They debuted as somebody else
eras.text: John Schroeder of Rockville took his stage name from a band called The Stab and built Government Issue around it. The first show went out as The Substitutes, the second got shut down by police, and by the end of 1981 there was a Dischord single and a Minor Threat member on bass.

years.h: Rockville's John Schroeder borrows a name and becomes John Stabb
years.p: [[John Stabb|898f9d0f-b024-45f4-b887-60aec4ba0eec]] recruits drummer Marc Alberstadt, guitarist John Barry and bassist Brian Gay to start Government Issue. The stage name comes from The Stab, a band Dischord says he claimed to have joined.

years.h: The first show goes out as The Substitutes
years.p: At the two-day Unheard Music Festival at D.C. Space, drummer Marc Alberstadt is sick and guests fill in. Police shut down the band's second show halfway through.
years.xp: Dischord's band history calls the fake name prophetic: by 1989 almost a dozen different people had joined and left, with Stabb the only original member still standing.

years.src: Dischord: Legless Bull · Wikipedia: Government Issue
years.h: Legless Bull goes out as Dischord No. 4
years.p: Ten songs, mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] at Inner Ear. For a year GI and [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] fought it out for top band in town.
years.xp: Steven Blush wrote that Legless Bull "best exemplified smartass suburban HC."

years.h: Gay leaves for college and Baker takes over on bass
years.p: With [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] on hiatus, [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] replaces Brian Gay in GI. Baker said later he joined the D.C. band he liked best that needed somebody.

years.h: Fear plays Saturday Night Live, and Tom Lyle plays bass
years.p: Halloween 1981: [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]] are on SNL with a D.C. crew slamming in the studio. [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] is one of them, so [[Tom Lyle|b61fd366-0bcb-4aae-bea7-c0152ca67584]] covers bass at GI's show.
years.xp:
Fear's appearance came about through John Belushi, and a crew of D.C. punks including [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] went up to New York to be the audience. That left GI a bassist short.

Lyle's night as a stand-in turned into the longest tenure in the band after Stabb's: bass, then guitar, and most of the music and cover art for the rest of the run.

years.h: Bass duty ends at the 9:30 Club, on a bill with T.S.O.L.
years.p: It's Brian Baker's final show as Government Issue's bassist, before he moves over to guitar.

eras.title: Tom Lyle takes the wheel
eras.text: Members came and went so fast that the core shrank to Stabb, Alberstadt and Tom Lyle, who moved to guitar, wrote most of the music and drew most of the covers. The songs got heavier and closer to rock, and Dischord released its first Government Issue album.

years.big: "I wasn't a bass player and Government Issue was a chance to play guitar."
q: I wasn't a bass player and Government Issue was a chance to play guitar.
years.h: John Barry leaves for Bulgaria, and Baker picks up a guitar
years.p: Guitarist John Barry moves to Bulgaria. [[Tom Lyle|b61fd366-0bcb-4aae-bea7-c0152ca67584]] takes bass full time.

years.h: Make an Effort comes out on Fountain of Youth
years.p: Brian Baker plays guitar and Tom Lyle bass on the EP. Baker later said the band was better with John Barry but bigger with Baker in it.

yt: Full set at the Wilson Center, June 1982
years.h: Baker goes back to Minor Threat once Stabb calms down
years.p: The parting is amicable, Baker said. [[Tom Lyle|b61fd366-0bcb-4aae-bea7-c0152ca67584]] moves to guitar and Mitch Parker comes in on bass.

years.h: Boycott Stabb is the small piece of a big session
years.p: In November 1982 [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produces GI at Inner Ear and they cut 20 songs, older ones included. Dischord releases only the newest.
years.xp: The line-up was John Stabb, Tom Lyle, Mitch Parker and Marc Alberstadt. The rest of the session waited decades and finally surfaced on side B of Dischord's white-vinyl Complete Session.

years.h: Joyride leaves Legless Bull far behind
years.p: Produced by Brian Baker, by then out of GI. Heavy and rocking, on Fountain of Youth.

years.h: Mike Fellows leaves GI for [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]]
years.p: Fellows is off to one of the bands about to rewrite D.C. punk. John Leonard takes over bass in GI.

eras.title: More than a hardcore band
eras.text: GI left Fountain of Youth for Mystic, recorded at CBGB, and pulled in goth, pop and psychedelia. Founding drummer Marc Alberstadt quit, former Minor Threat bassist Steve Hansgen arrived, and a joke about '70s prog turned into a real album.

years.h: The Fun Just Never Ends starts on the CBGB stage
years.p: Government Issue cut the basic tracks live at CBGB and finish them in a proper studio.

years.h: Mystic Records gets the next two GI releases
years.p: Looking for more push, the band leaves Fountain of Youth. Mystic puts out Give Us Stabb or Give Us Death and Live on Mystic.

years.h: Live at the CE Center, Philadelphia, February 23, 1985
yt: Live at the CE Center, Philadelphia, February 23, 1985

years.h: Marc Alberstadt, the last founder besides Stabb, quits mid-album
years.p: Drummer Alberstadt and bassist John Leonard both leave during the sessions for the self-titled album. Sean Saley takes the drums, and ex-Minor Threat bassist [[Steve Hansgen|cd469927-13a8-4d0b-8898-01c6856f5878]] joins.

years.h: Government Issue starts as a prog joke
years.p: Tom Lyle says it began as a concept album mocking '70s prog; the concept was dropped but the interludes stayed. John Stabb is singing melodies now, with a lot of [[The Damned|77d21c13-846f-4f48-9546-873949eff6ae]] in them.

eras.title: Big tours, then the wall
eras.text: With J. Robbins on bass and Peter Moffett on drums, GI made its last two albums for Giant and toured the US and Europe hard. The early hardcore crowd didn't follow, and a van crash in England helped end it.

years.cap: John Stabb and J. Robbins at Maxwell's, Hoboken, New Jersey, 1987
years.h: J. Robbins and Peter Moffett complete the last line-up
years.p: Sean Saley and Steve Hansgen are out after the self-titled record. [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] takes bass and Moffett the drums.

years.h: You is the first of two records for Giant
years.p: Giant also reissues GI's Fountain of Youth catalog. According to Wikipedia, You chronicled John Stabb's relationship with an underage girl.

years.cap: Released years later as Strange Wine: Live at CBGB
years.h: The CBGB tape sits for 16 years
years.p: GI's August 30, 1987 New York show turns up in 2003 as the live album Strange Wine, with Tom Lyle remastering the tapes himself.

years.h: Full set at the Hung Jury Pub, 1987
yt: Full set at the Hung Jury Pub, 1987

years.h: Crash ends the studio run on Giant
years.p: GI's widest-ranging album. Steven Blush's verdict was that the fans still wanted Legless Bull.

q: We felt we were beating our heads against the wall.
years.src: Wikipedia: Government Issue · Dischord: Government Issue
years.h: A van wreck in England ends the band
years.p: The accident shatters drummer Peter Moffett's ankle. Back home, Government Issue breaks up.
years.xp:
J. Robbins has been clear that the crash was only part of it. After huge tours of the US and Europe, the four of them looked at where things stood and saw they each wanted something different.

By the end almost a dozen people had passed through, and John Stabb was the only original member left. Robbins went on to [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]], and later reunited with Moffett in [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].

years.cap: Flyer for the farewell show at the 9:30 Club, June 1, 1989
years.h: The farewell show is at the 9:30 Club
years.p: The original run ends at the club where Brian Baker played his last GI bass show eight years earlier.
years.xp: The flyer reads Farewell Performance, Thursday, June 1st, 1989, with Edsel and Repercussion on the bill. J. Robbins remembered the night as "massive, ridiculous, and fun."

eras.title: The archive opens, and old bandmates show up
eras.text: Stabb went back to his given name and played in a string of D.C. bands while the catalog got collected and reissued. After he was assaulted in 2007, the old line-ups turned up to help.

years.h: Dr. Strange Records starts collecting the catalog
years.p: Complete History Volume One comes out in 2000. Volume Two follows in 2002.

years.src: Wikipedia: Government Issue · Wikipedia: John Stabb · Dischord: Government Issue
years.h: The assault, then a benefit under the name Government Re-Issue
years.p: On July 17, five men assault [[John Stabb|898f9d0f-b024-45f4-b887-60aec4ba0eec]] near his home and he needs extensive facial reconstruction surgery, Wikipedia reports. On September 23 he, Tom Lyle, Brian Baker and drummer William Knapp play a benefit for his medical bills and lost wages.
years.xp:
Help came from more than one direction. Part of the proceeds from the 2007 Riot Fest went to Stabb for his medical bills, and part to [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]], whose son had been diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy.

The Government Re-Issue name was the joke; the line-up was not. Stabb, Lyle and Baker had last shared a stage in the early '80s.

years.cap: John Stabb singing with Sleeper Agent at Fort Reno, Washington DC, July 2010
years.h: One more benefit for the last line-up
years.p: John Stabb, Tom Lyle, J. Robbins and Peter Moffett play D.C. as a benefit for local fan Steve 'Stereo Faith' McPherson.
years.xp: Stabb was singing with other D.C. bands by then. The photo shows him with Sleeper Agent at Fort Reno that July, five months before the benefit.

eras.title: Legless Bull, one more time
eras.text: Stabb, John Barry and Brian Gay brought the Legless Bull line-up back, with Karl Hill on drums, liked it and kept going. Stabb was on stage into the last months of his life.

years.h: GI shares a Black Cat bill with Dag Nasty
years.p: The December 28 show at D.C.'s Black Cat supports the Salad Days documentary, in which John Stabb appears. [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] is on the same bill.

q: Government Issue is a group again.
years.h: The Legless Bull line-up plays Damaged City
years.p: John Stabb, John Barry and Brian Gay reunite for D.C.'s Damaged City Festival, with Karl Hill on drums.
years.xp:
Thirty-three years after the first EP, the people who made it were back on a D.C. stage. Stabb said they had so much fun they'd keep it going: "Government Issue is a group again."

It stuck. GI played Houston's Bad Ass Weekend in February 2015 and a five-date Southeast run that fall, including The Fest.

years.cap: John Stabb with History Repeated at the Black Cat, Washington DC, June 2015
years.h: Stabb sings his last show with History Repeated
years.p: It's the final performance for [[John Stabb|898f9d0f-b024-45f4-b887-60aec4ba0eec]], in the band he formed in 2008. He dies less than four months later.

years.src: Wikipedia: John Stabb · Washington Post: John Stabb dies
years.h: John Stabb dies at 54 in Rockville
years.p: John Schroeder, 1961-2016, dies of stomach cancer in a hospice in Rockville, Maryland, where he grew up.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes a 112-day battle. On St. Patrick's Day that year he had married his longtime partner, Mina Devadas.
